PL-0902 adds 58 cases across stream-candidate.test.ts and stream-candidate.property.test.ts. THE DESIGN WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS CHOSEN: adding the field to streamCandidateSchema directly was tried and breaks typecheck in 11 files across 4 packages, none of them in this task's surface; that experiment was reverted before anything was written and is corroboration rather than the reason. The architectural reason is that streamCandidateSchema is the RANKER's input and DESKTOP_PLAYBACK section 4 rules that ranking may prefer a candidate only one adapter can play, so a score component discounting protected candidates would be a second opinion about routing living in the one component that must not hold one. Hence resolvedStreamCandidateSchema extends it and streamCandidateSchema is byte-for-byte unchanged. MUTATION-CHECKED FOUR WAYS, each caught and then restored: requiresContentDecryptionModule narrowed to === protected (3 failures), protection given a .default of clear (4), .strict() removed from the protected variant (2), and the licence URL allowed over http (2). Unknown is a MEMBER OF THE UNION rather than null or an absent field, deliberately -- null is the right spelling of unknown for a media fact, but every reader's reflex for a null DRM field is 'there is no DRM', and requiresContentDecryptionModule is written as state !== clear so a fourth state added later defaults to requiring a CDM rather than to a silent attempt. packages/contracts/src/testing/arbitraries.ts was NOT touched because PL-0206 is editing it; the generators are local to the property file and composed from the shared streamCandidateArb, with the follow-up named in the file.

assigned.title: DRM capability on the candidate and playback-session contract
assigned.description: packages/contracts/src contains no occurrence of drm, widevine, playready or eme -- verified by grep across the whole source tree on 2026-09-15. So a resolved candidate carries no statement about whether it is encrypted, under which system, or against which license server. PL-0901 makes that a blocking gap rather than a cosmetic one: the desktop build routes between an mpv adapter that has no CDM and cannot be given one, and a Shaka/EME adapter that has one, and PlayerAdapter.canPlay is required to return a REASON on both branches rather than a boolean guess. A reasoned decision cannot be made from a contract that carries no field to reason about, so this gates the capability routing in PL-0901 section 4.
assigned.notes: THE SHAPE IS A CAPABILITY DESCRIPTOR, NOT A BOOLEAN. An isDrm flag would answer the routing question and nothing else; the adapter also has to say WHY it refused, and a reason trail that says drm_required with no system named is not debuggable, which is invariant 4. The reviewer should expect at minimum the protection system and, where the boundary knows it, the license acquisition endpoint -- and should rule on whether an UNKNOWN encryption state is representable, because absent is not the same as none. A candidate whose encryption state was never established must not read as clear; that is the same required-and-nullable discipline PL-0207 established for media facts, and the precedent is deliberate. WHERE IT LIVES IS PART OF THE QUESTION. The descriptor could sit on streamCandidate, on the playback-session response, or on both with one deriving from the other. The candidate is what the ranker scores and the session is what the player is handed, and PL-0301's implementation already argues at packages/provider-sdk/src/fixture/provider.ts that the playable address belongs on the session rather than the candidate, for a reason that may or may not extend to the key system. Settle it before writing it. NOTHING HERE MAY WEAKEN A PROTECTION. This task describes encryption so the correct player is chosen and so a refusal is explainable. It adds no decryption, no key handling and no fallback that would attempt a protected source with an engine that has no CDM -- invariant 2 -- and the mpv adapter's refusal must stay a refusal rather than becoming a degraded attempt. SEQUENCING: overlaps PL-0206 and PL-AI-0006 on packages/contracts and must be sequenced after whichever is active. It should land before PL-0501 writes the session response, because retrofitting a discriminated field into a shipped contract is the change PL-0501's own acceptance warns about.
assigned.acceptance: A resolved stream candidate, or the playback session that carries it, states its content-protection requirement explicitly: the protection system where one applies, an unencrypted state that is asserted rather than inferred from an absent field, and an UNKNOWN state that is representable and does not read as unencrypted. PlayerAdapter.canPlay can decide routing from the contract alone, without inspecting a URL, a manifest or a provider-specific field, and can name the protection system in its refusal reason. Adding the field changes no existing candidate's meaning by accident: a candidate that omits it is refused by the schema rather than defaulted to clear. Provider-specific spellings stay inside @liberty/provider-sdk and are normalized before they reach the contract. No decryption, key handling or protection bypass is added.

recommended.title: Contract module boundaries
recommended.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes
